sun.upright:
Aries is cardinal fire, ruled by Mars, and an Aries Sun wants to be the one who goes first. So this is a slightly awkward card to draw for your light. The Page of Cups is the gentlest of the court cards, a young person in a flowered tunic staring into a cup because a fish has just put its head out, and nothing in that scene is in a hurry. Water and fire are opposed elements. When they meet you get steam, or one puts the other out.

From the inside it feels a bit like being caught out. You've got something tender going on, a feeling for someone, a creative idea, a wish you haven't told anyone, and it doesn't fit the version of yourself you usually lead with. Your instinct is to act on it straight away or brush it off as silly. The Emperor is Aries's own Major, all rules and authority, and this card is about as far from him as the deck gets. I see this a lot with Aries Suns, and it usually comes out as impatience with yourself for caring about something so small.

At work it might be a project you'd love to try that isn't the obviously ambitious move, the kind that would make you a beginner again for a while. With a partner, or someone you like, it's the soft thing you'd say if you weren't worried about sounding young. Give it a week before you decide anything. Tell one person about it, out loud, and listen to how it sounds.
sun.reversed:
Blocked, this card gives an Aries Sun a reason to decide feelings are a waste of time. The tender streak got embarrassed and went underground, and in a fire sign ruled by Mars that usually comes out sideways, as snappiness, as a sulk you'd never call a sulk, as pushing harder at the one thing you can control. Or it swings the other way and you're all feeling for a while, touchy and wounded, taking a bit of teasing much too personally.

Watch how you react to small criticism at work, and how you handle someone who wants you to be gentler with them. Before you answer the next thing that stings, wait long enough to work out whether you're hurt or angry. For an Aries the two are easy to confuse, and they need different replies.

moon.upright:
An Aries Moon usually gets its feelings over with fast. Something upsets you, you flare, you say so, and ten minutes later you've moved on and can't understand why everyone else is still upset. That's cardinal fire in the Moon, a sign ruled by Mars, feeling that turns straight into action. This card brings in a different kind of feeling altogether, one that arrives quietly and doesn't burn off. Fire and water are opposites, and the Page is all water.

It might be a soft spot for someone you can't shake, or a memory that keeps coming back at odd moments, or a sadness with no obvious cause that you'd honestly rather punch than sit with. The difficulty for an Aries Moon is that there's nothing to do with it. You can't fix it and you can't win it. It just wants to be felt, like a child holding up something they found and waiting for you to look. That can make you restless and short with people, and it isn't really about them.

Sleep is often where it catches up with you, late at night when you've finally stopped moving and the feeling's still there. It shows too in how you answer a partner or a sibling who asks what's wrong. Try telling them you don't know yet, that something's bothering you and you're still working out what.
moon.reversed:
When this Page lands upside down on an Aries Moon, the soft feeling gets no airtime at all. You're hurt, and it comes out as temper. You're lonely, and it comes out as being busy, booking things, starting a fight about the dishes. Mars rules the sign your Moon is in, and Mars would always prefer to move, so the feeling gets buried under all that activity and leaks out as irritability.

The other version is a mood that won't lift and that you're embarrassed by, so you hide it. Home is where either one shows first, with the person who knows you well enough to see through the busyness. Go for a long walk or a run, since your body is how an Aries Moon gets things moving, and somewhere in the second half of it ask yourself what actually upset you.

rising.upright:
With Aries rising you usually come through the door first and fast. People meet the Mars side of you before anything else, the directness, the quick decision, the look that says you're about to do something. Mars rules Aries, so it's the ruler of your whole chart, and that's a lot of forward push in how you start things. Drawing the Page of Cups for your mask puts a softer face over the top, and because fire and water are opposed they don't sit easily together.

People are catching you with your guard down, looking younger and softer. You might blush where you'd usually bluster. You ask a question where you'd normally state a view, or you let slip that you're nervous. Aries rising can find that exposing, because your whole approach to strangers relies on being ready before they are. But the instinct you're leading with is a curious one, and people can see it on your face.

That's a real advantage in a job interview or a first meeting with a new team, because people trust someone who looks interested. It's the same on a first date. Let the new face stay up a bit longer than feels comfortable. When you catch yourself about to take charge of a conversation, ask the other person one more question first.
rising.reversed:
Aries rising already reacts before it thinks, and a reversed Page adds hurt feelings to that reflex. Someone's short with you in the lift and you take it as a verdict. A comment in a meeting lands wrong and you bristle where everyone can see, then spend the afternoon replaying it. The face you're showing is thinner-skinned than usual, and with Mars running the chart it goes straight to defence.

It can also look like shyness covered with bravado, somewhere new especially, a party where you know one person, the first week of a job. People read it as prickly when it's nerves. Take a breath before you answer the next thing that feels like a slight. Most of them turn out to be about the other person's day, and you'll be glad you didn't bite.

sun.upright:
Something small and tender wants to be made, and a Taurus Sun is about the best person in the zodiac to make it. Taurus is fixed earth, ruled by Venus, built for things that last. You go at your own pace and like results you can hold. Water and earth get on, each giving the other shape and nourishment, so this is the kind of pairing where a soft beginning actually takes root.

What this Page brings to your Sun is a creative seed, usually something to do with beauty or the senses, food, music, fabric, the garden, which is Venus territory anyway. You might be surprised by how much you want to make something that isn't useful, just nice. That can feel slightly silly to a sign that likes to justify its time. It isn't silly. Taurus has the patience to take a soft start and keep feeding it until it's real. The Hierophant is Taurus's Major, the card of teachers and tradition, and there's often a pull toward learning a craft properly, from someone who knows it.

It might be a class you keep looking at online, or a side project that could carry a price tag eventually. In a relationship it's the urge to court someone again, a meal, flowers, a letter. Pick one of those and do the first small version of it, the one that costs almost nothing.
sun.reversed:
Comfort tends to stand in for creativity when this Page is reversed for a Taurus Sun. You had the idea, you liked it, and then you stayed on the sofa with it. Fixed earth is good at keeping things, and that includes keeping a dream exactly where it is, safe and undisturbed and never started. Sometimes it's sentimentality, holding on to how something used to feel and being quietly hurt that it's changed.

Look at your money and your possessions. You buy the materials and don't use them, or you spend on small treats to fill a feeling you haven't named. In a long relationship you might miss the early sweetness and sulk about it privately, which Taurus does very well. Choose the smallest piece of the idea and give it one hour on a day you'd otherwise waste.

moon.upright:
Think of the look on the Page's face in the Rider-Waite card, a young person holding a cup while a fish peers out of it, pleased and not at all alarmed. That's roughly what a Taurus Moon does with a gentle feeling when it's given time. Your Moon is in fixed earth, ruled by Venus, and it needs steadiness, the familiar bed, the same good bread, people who don't change on you. Earth and water are friendly elements, so this card sits comfortably in your tides.

What arrives is soft. A fondness for someone, growing slowly. A wish to make the house nicer. Old music. None of it's dramatic, and it doesn't need to be, because a Taurus Moon processes through the body and the senses, and a feeling this size is one you can hold in your hands and look at. You may find you're easily moved, tearing up at a film, going quiet over a smell that reminds you of a grandparent. Taurus Moons are sentimental underneath, whatever they let on.

In the body, it helps to eat slowly and sleep properly and let yourself be comforted without making a project of it. With someone close, it's small gestures, cooking for them, a hand on their back. Let someone look after you for an evening, and don't tidy up first.
moon.reversed:
A feeling that had nowhere else to go has probably gone into the body. With a Taurus Moon and this card reversed, you're comfort-eating, or oversleeping, or buying things you didn't need, and if anyone asks, you're fine. Fixed earth holds on, and what it's holding is a small hurt or a disappointment you decided wasn't worth mentioning. It hasn't gone away. It's settled in.

Evenings are when it's easiest to spot, when the routine is doing too much of the soothing. In a relationship it can turn into a slow, stubborn sulk that Taurus is very good at and rarely owns up to. Name the small thing to the person it concerns, even if it sounds petty. Taurus can let go of almost anything once it's been said out loud, plainly, once.

rising.upright:
Taurus rising makes Venus the ruler of your chart, and it usually gives a calm, unhurried first impression. You look like someone who won't be rushed, and people tend to relax near you. With the Page of Cups over that, the calm picks up a sweeter edge. Water and earth are good company for each other, so there's no clash, just a softening, and strangers are likely to read you as kind and a little romantic.

It changes how you start things. You might be the one who makes the first friendly move, which fixed earth doesn't often do, or you say something warm to someone you've only just met and mean it. There can be a new interest in how you look, a colour you'd not normally wear, a softer cut, something the Page would approve of, given that flowered tunic. It's partly vanity, and you know it, and partly wanting the outside to match a gentler mood. People pick up on it, and some of them will want to get closer.

At work someone may bring you a personal problem because you seem safe. In dating, your usual slow approach might meet someone who moves quicker than you do. Let the pace stay yours. Say yes to one invitation you'd normally think over for a week.
rising.reversed:
Withdrawal can pass for calm with Taurus rising, and with the Page reversed that's usually what's happening. You seem pleasant and unbothered, and underneath you're a bit hurt, or shy, or not sure you're wanted, so you don't make the first move and then feel left out when nobody else does either. Venus rules your chart, and the reversed card can turn that Venus side into waiting to be courted, by friends and colleagues as much as by lovers.

At gatherings you stay near the food and the one person you know. In a new job you take months to say anything personal. Nobody can tell you'd like to be asked. Make one small warm move first, a message, a compliment, an offer of tea, and notice how quickly people meet you once you do.

sun.upright:
The Page of Cups was always a messenger card, the young one sent ahead with news, and Gemini is ruled by Mercury, the messenger planet. So on the face of it you should get on. The difference is in what's being carried. Gemini is mutable air and deals in ideas and information and the fun of knowing a bit about everything, and this Page carries a feeling. Air and water are neutral to each other. They don't fight, and they don't mix on their own either.

For a Gemini Sun that often means trying to understand something you actually need to feel. You notice you've been talking about a person or a plan for weeks, turning it over, collecting opinions, and it's still not settled, because the part that needs settling isn't a thought. The Lovers is Gemini's Major, a card about choosing with the heart, and that's a fair hint. What you want to make of yourself might be plainer and more sincere for a while, which to a Gemini can feel quite exposed.

It shows in writing, a story or a letter or a message that says what you mean without a joke at the end to cover it. It shows with siblings and old friends, where you can risk being earnest. Write one thing by hand, for someone, and give it to them.
sun.reversed:
Turned over, this card gives a Gemini Sun a clever way of never saying what it feels. You're funny about it. You change the subject. You've got four theories about why you're upset and none of them involves actually being upset. Mutable air can move away from anything, and the tender thing just waits by the door while you talk.

Or it goes the other way and you're oversharing, telling everyone about the crush or the hurt, collecting opinions and getting no closer to knowing what you want. Both versions live in your phone, in the text you edit ten times, in the group chat where you turn it into a bit. Say the feeling once, plainly, to the one person it's about. Then give it a rest with everyone else for a while.

moon.upright:
Talking is how a Gemini Moon calms down. You work out how you feel by saying it, messaging someone, reading about it, getting it into words, and once it's in words you can usually let it go. This Page brings the kind of feeling that doesn't come with words attached. A hunch. A mood that drifts in with a song. A soft spot for someone you've only chatted to twice. Water and air have no natural way of talking to each other, and your Moon has to do the introducing.

You may notice you're restless without knowing why. Mercury rules Gemini, and Mercury wants a label, so it'll keep offering explanations, tiredness, the weather, that thing someone said, and none of them quite fits. The Page's feeling is young and it hasn't got a name yet. Pin one on it too fast and you lose what it was trying to tell you. Gemini Moons are often better at this than they give themselves credit for. You're curious by nature, and curiosity is exactly what this card asks for.

At night it can show up as busy, vivid dreams, the sort you want to tell someone about over breakfast. With friends it might be a conversation that turns tender without warning. Next time a feeling turns up with no reason attached, describe it to yourself the way you'd describe a stranger, and leave it unsolved.
moon.reversed:
Feelings get talked to death when a Gemini Moon draws this card reversed. You explain it, analyse it, send three friends the screenshots, and every conversation leaves you a little more wound up. Some of the friends are getting tired of it, too, which you've half noticed. Mutable air keeps things moving, which is normally how you cope, but a Page of Cups feeling is small and shy and doesn't survive that much handling.

The other version is nervous restlessness you can't account for, flicking between apps at midnight, never settling to anything. Sleep is usually the first thing to go, then your patience with whoever you live with. Put the phone in another room for one evening. Sit with the feeling for ten minutes without describing it to anyone, and see whether it changes on its own.

rising.upright:
Gemini rising usually meets people with a question and a joke. You're quick, curious, a bit restless, easy to talk to, and strangers often guess you're younger than you are. That's Mercury ruling the chart, the planet of noticing and chatting and moving on. The Page fits the youthful look almost too well. Where you differ is that you're curious about everything, and the Page is curious about one thing, the fish looking back out of the cup, and is happy to keep staring at it.

So the mask softens and slows down a little. People may notice you listening, or catch a moment where you're completely absorbed in what someone's telling you. Air and water don't clash and don't naturally blend either, so there can be an odd feeling of running at two speeds, the chatter carrying on while something quieter watches. You'll probably come across as sincere, and people open up faster to that.

It's handy in a new job, where people will tell you how things really work. It matters in romance too, since you're likely to be read as sweet and a bit dreamy, which gets a different kind of attention from the usual. When someone new starts telling you something personal, don't reach for the quip. Ask how they felt about it.
rising.reversed:
Flaky is how Gemini rising can read with this card reversed. You say you'll come and don't, you start a conversation warmly and drift off mid-sentence, and people aren't sure whether you like them. Often what's going on is shyness in a fast costume. Mercury runs your chart, and when the Page is upside down the chatter covers for a softness you're not ready to show a stranger.

First dates stay jokey and never get anywhere. In meetings you over-promise to seem keen. Or you swing the other way and tell a near stranger far too much. Pick one person you've been half-friendly with for a while and have one proper conversation with them, phone away, where you both ask and answer something real.

sun.upright:
Cancer is one of the three signs this card is made of. The Page of Cups carries the whole of water in its youngest form, Cancer and Scorpio and Pisces together, so with a Cancer Sun you're reading a card that already speaks your language. Cancer is cardinal water, ruled by the Moon, and it starts things through feeling. Everything the card does, it does in your key, and that turns it up, for good and for a bit too much.

What you're building in yourself is a softer kind of confidence. Cancer Suns tend to take care of everyone, and the Page brings back the part of you that's still being taken care of, the child who's delighted by small things and hurt by small things too. You may find you're sentimental in a way you'd tease someone else for, keeping tickets, photographing everything, getting attached quickly. That's lovely. It also needs a little watching, because a cardinal water sign with its own element doubled can start whole projects on the strength of one mood, and you'll probably do that at least once.

At home it can show as a wish to make the place feel properly yours. With family, it might be a younger relative who reminds you of yourself, or a parent you're seeing differently. Make one thing with your hands for the house, badly if need be, and keep it.
sun.reversed:
Hurt pride is the usual shape of this for a Cancer Sun. Somebody didn't notice what you did for them, or forgot something that mattered, and instead of saying so you've gone into your shell to see how long it takes them to notice. The Moon rules Cancer, and a doubled water card turned over tends to mean feeling that circles, going round and round the same small slight until it's much bigger than it was.

Family is where it's most visible, and the friends who count as family. It can also sit in a creative idea you've shelved because someone was lukewarm about it once. Tell the person what you needed from them, in one sentence, without the history attached. Then take the shelved idea out and look at it again with nobody else in the room.

moon.upright:
The Moon rules Cancer, so a Cancer Moon is the Moon in its own sign, and your feelings are already the loudest thing in your chart most days. Then this card turns up for your tides, water in its freshest form. It's the same element on the same element, and Cancer is inside the card's own home ground. Nothing here is fighting, so there's no brake on it either.

You'll probably notice it as memory. Old songs, your mum's kitchen, a smell in a hallway, a school friend who pops into your head for no reason. Cancer Moons keep everything, and the Page tends to open the drawers. It can be sweet, and it can also be a lot, particularly when you're tired, because cardinal water doesn't just feel, it wants to act on the feeling, ring the old friend, redo the spare room, bake for everybody. Some of that is lovely and some of it is you trying to soothe yourself by looking after other people.

In the body it tends to follow your sleep and your appetite, so eat properly and go to bed at a sensible hour. With family, there can be a real tenderness, and a chance to say something kind you've been holding. Choose one of the old feelings that's come up and follow it through with the person it belongs to.
moon.reversed:
Reversed on a Cancer Moon, this Page tends to mean feelings with nowhere to go, so they go round. You're moody and you know it. Small things land hard, a short reply, a plan changed at the last minute, and you take them to heart and then withdraw. Cancer Moons are good at carrying on looking after everyone through a mood like this, which is partly why nobody notices. With water doubled on the Moon's own sign, flooding is the risk, and with the card upside down the flood happens privately, behind a shut door.

Home shows it first, especially in how you are with the people you live with, and it can show in your sleep and appetite too. Don't go digging in the past for the reason. Ask what you need this evening, one specific thing, and ask someone for it directly.

rising.upright:
Behind the friendliness of Cancer rising there's usually a shell. The Moon rules your chart, and it gives you a careful way into things. You're warm, but you size people up first, and you let them in once you know they're safe. The Page of Cups is water too, and Cancer sits inside this card's own zone, so the fit is close. What changes is the shell. For a while, the face you meet the world with has less of it.

People can see what you're feeling. You smile at strangers, you get teary at a friend's speech, you say 'oh, that's lovely' out loud when you'd usually just think it. Cardinal water leads with feeling, and with this card over the top the lead is unguarded, a bit young, easy to read. Some people find that very endearing. Others take a little advantage of it, and Cancer rising can tell which is which quickly once it's paying attention.

Strangers may confide in you, on a train, in a queue, in the first week at a new job. With someone you're getting to know, your openness might move things along faster than your usual pace, and that's alright. Keep one small thing back for yourself each time, something you haven't told anyone, so the openness stays something you're choosing.
rising.reversed:
When the Page is upside down over Cancer rising, the shell comes back up and gets thicker. You seem polite and distant, or you seem fine and then go quiet in a way people notice. Sometimes it's a mood on your face that you think you're hiding and aren't. How you meet people already follows how you feel, with the Moon ruling your chart, and a reversed Page means the feeling is sore and a bit sulky.

It shows in first meetings where you decide someone doesn't like you before they've had a chance to, and in the way you pull back at work after one tactless remark. Go to the next thing anyway, the drinks or the meeting, and stay twenty minutes longer than you want to before you decide how it went.

sun.upright:
Leo is fixed fire and the only sign the Sun rules, so a Leo Sun is built to be seen. You want your work and your warmth to land, and you'd like some credit for it. This card is a very different sort of light, a young person in a fancy outfit gazing at a fish in a cup, absorbed and performing for nobody. Water and fire are opposite elements, and with a Leo Sun that friction usually turns into a question about being watched.

You've got something tender and new on the go, a creative idea, a feeling for someone, a hobby you're no good at yet. Part of you wants to make it big and show everyone. Part of you would die if anyone saw the first draft. Fixed fire likes to hold its shape, and a new feeling doesn't have one yet, so you can end up protecting your pride by never starting. I've seen that in a lot of Leo Suns. They'd prefer to wait until they're good.

In creative work this is permission to be an amateur and enjoy it. With children, or with someone you're courting, it's the playful, silly side of you that forgets how it looks. Do one creative thing where nobody's watching, and don't post it anywhere.
sun.reversed:
Reversed with a Leo Sun, the Page usually means wounded pride dressed up as not caring. Someone didn't clap, or clapped for someone else, and you've quietly decided the whole thing was beneath you. The warmth goes out a bit. Fire and water are at odds anyway, and with the card upside down it's the water winning. You can seem sulky, or showy in a hollow way, putting on a bigger performance to cover a feeling that's actually quite small and sore.

Leo doesn't like being seen to need things. You'll find this in creative work you've stopped sharing, and with a partner whose attention you want and won't ask for. Ask for it. Say you'd love them to see something you've made, and let them see it before it's finished.

moon.upright:
There's a small, soft need in this draw that a Leo Moon doesn't always admit to. Leo Moons need to feel special to someone. You want warmth and loyalty and a bit of fuss, and when you get it you give it back twice over. This card brings the younger version of that need, the part that wants to be noticed and is shy about asking. Your Moon is in fixed fire, ruled by the Sun, and the card is water, the opposing element, so what you get inside is a bit of steam.

It feels like wanting extra affection and being embarrassed about it. You might go quiet to see if anyone notices. You might get oddly emotional over a kind word from a friend, or a child saying something sweet, and have to leave the room. Fixed fire likes its feelings big and clear, and this is small and wobbly, so you may not trust it. Then you're cross with yourself for making a fuss, which doesn't help.

It shows most with a partner, where you might want to be looked after for once, and with close friends, where you notice who checks in. Your body may want rest and warmth, a bath, sun on your face. Ask one person for the attention you want, in plain words, and let them give it.
moon.reversed:
A Leo Moon with this card reversed can get very dramatic about a very small hurt. Somebody forgot to reply, and by evening it's become proof that nobody really cares. Fire and water fight when they meet, and the upside-down Page lets the steam build until it comes out as a scene, or as a cold, proud silence that's meant to be noticed. Leo Moon feelings are honest. They're just very large.

Partners and close friends get the brunt of it, and sometimes a parent, the one person who always gets the drama. It can also make you sulk over creative work that didn't get the praise you hoped for. Check how you're sleeping and eating before you decide anyone's let you down. If you're still hurt the next day, say what happened in one plain sentence and skip the speech.

rising.upright:
Look at how the Page is dressed in the Rider-Waite deck. The tunic is covered in flowers, there's a hat with a long scarf trailing off it, and the whole outfit is a bit much for someone standing by the sea looking at a fish. Leo rising would approve. With the Sun ruling your chart you tend to make an entrance, warm and noticeable, and people usually clock you before you've said anything.

This card changes the flavour of that entrance. Fixed fire leading the way usually looks confident. Put water in front of it, the opposite element, and the confidence gets a nervous shimmer underneath. You might feel shy walking into rooms you'd normally own. Or you might end up the charming, slightly dreamy one instead of the star, and find people warm to that faster. Strength belongs to Leo among the Majors, and there's something of that card's gentleness in how you're coming across, a softness that doesn't need to push.

It can do a lot for you at work, especially if you're new or pitching an idea, because people trust someone who seems sincere. On a date it's the open, playful side of you that wins. Before you go into the next room full of people, drop the plan for how you'll come across and walk in curious about one person there.
rising.reversed:
Leo rising with a reversed Page can come across as needy without meaning to. You walk in looking for a reaction, and if the room doesn't give you one quickly you either turn up the charm or go cool and aloof. Underneath it's usually a young, uncertain feeling, a worry that nobody's pleased to see you. With the Sun ruling your chart, how you're received matters to you more than you let on.

Parties and new jobs bring it out, and so does social media, where it's very easy to check who's noticed you. It can show in how you dress, too, going big to hide feeling small. Go somewhere and ask three people questions before you say anything about yourself. Leo rising is very likeable when it's interested in someone else.

sun.upright:
A first draft is the hardest thing in the world for a Virgo Sun to show anyone, and this Page is more or less a first draft of a feeling. Virgo is mutable earth, ruled by Mercury. You want to be useful, you want to be good at what you do, and you like to see the thing working before you put your name on it. Water and earth are friendly elements, so there's no fight here. Things you start under this card have a good chance of lasting.

The tension is all about getting it right. You've got an idea, or a new interest, or a tender feeling about someone, and your instinct is to research it and improve it before you let it out. That can kill a young idea. Mutable earth bends, though, and when you let yourself be a beginner you learn quickly and happily. The Hermit is Virgo's Major, the one who goes off alone with a lantern to work something out, and there's a version of that here, a private project done for its own sake.

It might be a craft or a course, something with your hands. It might be a friend who needs you to be gentle with them for a bit and to stop suggesting fixes. Make something small and imperfect and give it to someone before you've tidied it up.
sun.reversed:
Criticism aimed inward is how the reversed Page usually looks for a Virgo Sun. You had a soft, hopeful idea and you've picked it apart until there's nothing left to like. Or you've stopped feeling much about your work at all, because feeling about it made you anxious. Mercury rules Virgo, and with the card turned over that busy Mercury mind talks you out of every tender instinct before it's had a chance.

At work it looks like fussing over details on a project you secretly don't care about any more. In the body it can show as tension, a tight jaw, a stomach that knots when you're worried. Pick the idea you dismissed and give it an honest twenty minutes without editing anything. Then leave it alone overnight.

moon.upright:
Virgo Moons calm down by sorting things. A tidy drawer, a list, a problem solved for a friend, a routine that runs the way it should. Your Moon is in mutable earth, ruled by Mercury, and your feelings often come through the body and the small rhythms of the day. This Page brings a softer, younger kind of feeling into that, and because water and earth nourish each other it tends to go well, as long as you don't try to file it.

What you may notice is hunches. Your body is telling you things before your head gets there, a tiredness that means you need a break, a lift in your chest around someone new, an uneasy feeling about a plan. Virgo Moons are often very intuitive and don't call it that, because it doesn't feel mystical. It feels like noticing. This card asks you to trust that noticing a bit further, even when you can't give reasons. That's hard for a sign that likes to check its working.

Your daily routine might want a gentler rhythm, more walking, fewer screens. At work, it can show in how you respond to a junior colleague or someone who's struggling. Pick one hunch you've had recently and act on it without checking it with anyone first.
moon.reversed:
When the Page turns over on a Virgo Moon, feeling tends to come out as worry. You can't say you're sad or lonely, so you're anxious about the car, the bills, the gutters, your friend's tone in a message. Mutable earth copes by fixing, and this reversed card is a feeling that doesn't want fixing, so you keep finding new things to fix. It's hard to spot from inside, because it looks a lot like being responsible.

Sleep goes first, lying awake running through lists, and then you get critical with the people you live with over small domestic things. Set a time each evening, ten minutes, when you let yourself feel whatever's there without doing anything about it. Then go and do something with your hands.

rising.upright:
Neat, sharp and a little reserved is how strangers tend to read Virgo rising. You notice everything, you're polite, and you don't give much away until you've worked people out. Mercury rules your chart, so your first move is to observe. The Page of Cups softens the front you're putting up. Earth and water work well together, so this isn't a clash, and people see someone thoughtful who's also quietly kind, and maybe a bit shy.

That shyness can be charming. You may catch yourself asking a new person about something that clearly matters to them, remembering the detail and bringing it up later, and they'll feel noticed in a way that sticks. The instinct you're leading with is a caring one, which Virgo rising always has but doesn't always show at first. It can make you look younger or less sure of yourself. That's fine. People open up to someone who doesn't seem to be judging them.

At work that makes you easy to approach, and newer staff may come to you with questions. With friends or on a date, the small attentive things you do will land better than anything clever you say. Let the softness show a bit sooner than you'd normally allow. When you notice something kind, say it.
rising.reversed:
Prim or stand-offish is how Virgo rising can come across with this card reversed, when really you're nervous. You tidy yourself up so carefully for a new situation that no warmth gets through, or you notice everything that's wrong in a room and it shows on your face. Mercury rules your chart, and in this reversal it's on guard, correcting and assessing when it'd be better off curious.

Interviews and first meetings bring it out, and the first few weeks of anything new, where you come across as cooler than you are. Some of it is fear of getting it wrong in front of people. Try letting one small thing be imperfect on purpose, arriving without the notes, wearing the shirt that's a bit creased, and see who's friendlier.

sun.upright:
Of all the court cards, the Page of Cups is the one most often read as a love letter, and a Libra Sun is ruled by Venus, so there's an obvious link. Libra is cardinal air. You tend to find yourself through other people, making things fair and pleasant and beautiful, and you'd like to be liked for it. The less obvious part is the element. Air and water are neither friends nor enemies, and for a Libra Sun that shows up as the gap between being charming and saying what you actually feel.

The Page wants the second one. Something tender is going on, maybe a new attraction, maybe a creative idea you love more than you've admitted, maybe a realisation about what you want from a friendship. Cardinal air starts things through conversation and balance, so your instinct is to check how it'll land, weigh it up, make sure nobody's put out. Justice is Libra's Major and it holds scales for a reason. The Page isn't weighing anything up, and you might find that a relief.

In love, that could mean making the first move without a strategy. In creative work, it could mean making something just because you think it's lovely. Say one honest, warm thing to someone this week without softening it first.
sun.reversed:
Turned upside down for a Libra Sun, the Page often means a feeling you're keeping pleasant. You like someone and play it cool. You're hurt and you say it's fine. You love an idea and wait to see whether anyone else does first. Venus rules Libra, and the reversal tends to bend that Venus side toward keeping people happy at the cost of saying anything real.

Sometimes it flips into romantic daydreaming instead, a crush you've built a whole story around with no conversation to back it up. You'll see it in relationships, and in creative work you keep adjusting for an imagined audience. Take one feeling you've been smoothing over and say it plainly to the person concerned. Let there be a moment of awkwardness afterwards, and don't rush in to fix it.

moon.upright:
Things need to be nice for a Libra Moon, and not in a shallow way. You genuinely feel settled when the people around you are getting on and the room looks good, and unsettled when they aren't. Your Moon sits in cardinal air, ruled by Venus, and it tends to look after its feelings by looking after the relationship. This card brings in a feeling that belongs just to you, soft and new and a bit private. Air and water don't clash, but nothing joins them up either.

So you might be carrying a feeling you can't share yet. A small crush that would complicate things. A longing for something beautiful, music, art, a place by the water. A wish for a partner to be more romantic, which you haven't said because it might upset the balance. Libra Moons often talk themselves out of their own feelings by imagining the other person's side first. This card asks you to stay on your own side for a minute and notice what's there.

With a partner or a close friend, you may want more tenderness and have to ask for it. In your spare time, you might be drawn to galleries, pretty things, films that make you cry. Next time someone asks how you are, answer for yourself before you think about how they'll take it.
moon.reversed:
A reversed Page on a Libra Moon usually means a feeling that's been politely put away. You didn't want to upset anyone, so you agreed, and there's a little knot of resentment you're not proud of. Or you've drifted into a romantic fantasy that's much nicer to spend time in than the actual relationship. Cardinal air likes to act for the sake of balance, and with this card upside down you're keeping the peace and paying for it inside.

Look at the relationship where you do most of the smoothing over, and at any vague low mood you've put down to the weather. Notice the next time you say you don't mind and you do. Go back to that person the same day and tell them what you'd have preferred.

rising.upright:
Libra rising already has good manners and a pleasant face for strangers. Venus rules your chart, and you tend to meet people with charm, a bit of polish, an easy way of making them comfortable. The Page of Cups doesn't take any of that away. It makes it sweeter and younger and less practised. Air and water need introducing to each other, and here what gets introduced is feeling into the charm, so people get the sense you actually mean it.

Your face may give you away more, delight, embarrassment, interest, all showing before you've decided to show them. Strangers may flirt with you. Colleagues may tell you about a creative thing they're working on, because you look like someone who'd be pleased to hear it. Cardinal air leads with connection, and the connection you're offering is softer and less managed. Some Libra risings find that uncomfortable, because the charm was also a bit of protection.

In a new job, it can make you the person everyone likes quickly. On a date, it can make things move fast in a good way. It's also a good card for any work where you deal with the public, hospitality, sales, teaching, since people can feel that the warmth is real. Let one person see you slightly flustered, and don't cover it with a joke.
rising.reversed:
Too much sweetness is the usual trouble when Libra rising gets this card reversed. You smile at everyone, agree with everyone, and leave the room slightly exhausted and not sure anyone met you. Or it goes the other way and you're oddly touchy, hurt that someone didn't respond to your warmth, reading coolness where there wasn't any. With Venus ruling your chart, being liked can start to feel urgent. It's tiring, and it's usually because you're unsure of your footing underneath.

New social settings and early dating are where it shows, since you can end up shaping yourself to whoever's in front of you. At work it can look like saying yes to every request. In the next conversation where you'd normally agree just to be pleasant, give your real opinion, kindly, and see what happens.

sun.upright:
Two kinds of water meet in this draw. Scorpio is fixed water, ruled by Mars and in the modern view by Pluto, and it's one of the three signs this card is built from, so the elements don't clash at all. What clashes is age. The Page is water at its youngest and most trusting, and a Scorpio Sun is water that has been down to the bottom and knows what's there. You're reading your own element, doubled, in a form you might have outgrown a long time ago.

For you, the card brings back a kind of innocence. A feeling that doesn't need testing. An attraction you'd usually investigate for a while before trusting, arriving openly, and you find you're trusting it anyway. That's exposing for a sign that likes to know where the power sits. Fixed water holds on hard, and you may be holding on to an old guardedness that isn't needed with this person or this project. Death is Scorpio's card in the Majors, the one about endings that make room, and there can be a quiet version of that here. Some suspicion you've carried for years may just be ready to go.

It might show in a relationship where you're letting yourself be playful. It might show in creative work, something private you've never shown anyone. Let one person see something you'd normally keep back, and don't test them afterwards to see what they do with it.
sun.reversed:
With a Scorpio Sun, the reversed Page often looks like hurt turned into strategy. Something tender got bruised, a gesture that wasn't returned, a confidence that got passed on, and instead of admitting you were hurt you've gone cool, watchful, a bit punishing. Fixed water holds on, and with the card's water doubled on your own, the feeling doesn't drain away. Scorpio can hold a small hurt for a very long time and call it self-respect.

Close relationships show it, and friendships where you've started keeping score. So does a creative idea you won't share in case someone doesn't take it seriously. Tell the person you've gone cool on what actually stung, in a sentence or two, and say it while it's still small.

moon.upright:
Scorpio Moons feel everything all the way down and show very little of it. You need to trust people before you let them near, and once you do it's total. Your Moon is in fixed water, and this card is water too, from inside its own zone, so the Page is speaking a language you know well. The difference is that the Page's feelings are light and new and fairly easy to read, and yours usually aren't.

What this draw can bring is a feeling you don't know what to do with, because it isn't heavy. A small delight. A soft affection for someone that doesn't come with any fear attached. You may keep waiting for the catch. Fixed water holds its feelings for a long time, and when the element doubles up like this you'll either feel the sweetness very strongly or brood on it until it gets complicated. I've watched Scorpio Moons turn a lovely crush into an investigation within a week, and it's always a shame.

It can come up in sleep, vivid dreams, feelings surfacing at three in the morning. It comes up in intimacy too, where you might be sweet and playful in a way you usually save for very few people. Let a good feeling be good for a few days before you examine it.
moon.reversed:
Reversed, a Page of Cups on a Scorpio Moon tends to show as brooding. A small hurt goes deep and stays there. You replay a conversation, read into a message, and build a quiet case against someone who probably has no idea anything's wrong. The doubled water makes it intense, and the fixed quality makes it hard to shift.

It can also show as jealousy, or as checking up on people more than you'd like to admit. At home you get withdrawn, and in a relationship you might test the other person without telling them there's a test. Pick the one small thing that hurt and say it to whoever did it, even if it sounds minor out loud. Scorpio Moons usually feel a lot lighter once it's said.

rising.upright:
Intense is the word strangers usually reach for with Scorpio rising. You watch people carefully, you give away very little, and there's a steadiness in how you look at them that some find magnetic and some find unnerving. Mars rules Scorpio, so it rules your chart, with Pluto as the modern co-ruler, and that makes your first move a guarded one. This Page is water, like you, and your rising sign is part of the card's own territory, so it sits naturally. It just lightens the face.

People might see you curious and pleased and a bit open, which throws those who know you. You laugh sooner. You let someone see you're interested. There's still depth behind it, since fixed water doesn't stop being deep because the surface has calmed, and the first impression you're making is gentler and far more approachable. It can feel like going out without your usual coat on. Some Scorpio risings hate that, and some find it a relief.

In a new workplace, people who'd normally keep their distance may come and talk to you. In romance, someone might see the sweet side of you early. Let the lighter face stay for a few meetings with someone new before the guard comes back up, and see what they tell you.
rising.reversed:
Sulky or secretive is how Scorpio rising can come across with the Page reversed, even when you think you're being perfectly pleasant. There's a hurt you're carrying, and it shows as a closed look, short answers, a wariness people take personally. With Mars ruling the chart and the water turned upside down, you go into defence very quickly.

It shows most when you meet someone who reminds you of someone who let you down, and at work when you've been caught off guard. People may think you're judging them when you're protecting yourself. Now and then it flips into a sudden overshare with a near stranger that you regret the next day. Try smiling first, before you've made up your mind about someone, and let them earn the rest in the usual way.

sun.upright:
Sagittarius Suns are built for the long view. Mutable fire, ruled by Jupiter, you want to go somewhere, learn something, find out what it all means, and you're generous and funny while you do it. The Page of Cups draws you in close instead. Everything about it is small and near. Fire and water are opposing elements, and for a Sagittarius Sun that friction usually shows up as restlessness about something tender.

You might have a feeling you'd quite like to outrun. An attachment that would tie you down a bit. A creative idea that needs sitting still with. A sensitivity you'd normally laugh off. The tricky part is that mutable fire can always find a reason to move, and the Page doesn't want to go anywhere. It wants to stay and look. Temperance is the Major that belongs to Sagittarius, an angel pouring water from one cup into another, and your sign is quite capable of mixing fire and water. It just has to slow down enough to do it.

In study it might be a subject that moves you personally, even if it won't impress anyone. With a friend or partner, it might be the hard conversation they need you to stay for. Stay. Pick a place close to home and spend an afternoon there with no plan, and notice what you feel when you're not heading anywhere.
sun.reversed:
With a Sagittarius Sun, the Page upside down often means escaping a feeling by getting busy with the big picture. You're planning the trip, reading the book, starting the course, and not looking at the small sad or tender thing sitting in the corner. Jupiter rules your sign and can make anything bigger, including the story you tell yourself about why you're fine. Sometimes the optimism is a way of not stopping.

It can come out as tactlessness too, a joke that lands on someone's soft spot, and you honestly don't see it until later. Close friends and family feel it most. When someone goes quiet after one of your jokes, ask them about it, and be ready to hear that it stung.

moon.upright:
Space is what a Sagittarius Moon needs most. Room to move, something to look forward to, a bit of optimism in the air. When you're upset you tend to go outside, or book something, or talk it through until you've found the funny side. This card is water, and your Moon sits in mutable fire, so these are elements that don't naturally get along. What the Page brings into your tides is a small, close feeling, and small close feelings are the ones a Sag Moon finds hardest.

It might be homesickness, even if you're at home. It might be a longing for someone, or a shy new attachment that makes you want to stay in when you'd usually go out. You might be moved by something spiritual or beautiful in a way you can't quite explain, which you'll either love or quickly turn into a philosophy. Jupiter rules your Moon's sign, and Jupiter makes things larger, so even a small feeling can feel huge for a day and then vanish. It's worth catching before it goes.

At night it can show as restlessness. With friends you may want the ones who'll just sit with you. Let yourself stay in one evening you'd normally fill, and do something quiet and a bit sentimental, old photos, a long phone call with someone far away.
moon.reversed:
A Sagittarius Moon with a reversed Page tends to run from the feeling. You're not sad, you're just busy. You're not lonely, you're planning a trip. The tender thing gets no room because mutable fire is always looking over the horizon. Sometimes it goes the other way and you get uncharacteristically moody and don't know what to do with yourself.

Watch how often you're out of the house, and listen if a partner or friend says you've been a bit distant. Sleep can suffer too, lying awake with a restlessness you can't place. When you next feel the urge to book something or go somewhere, wait a day first. Ask what you'd be leaving behind in the room, and whether it's worth sitting with for an evening.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising meets the world like it's about to be an adventure. You're friendly, open, a bit loud sometimes, and you tend to say what you think before you've checked how it'll go down. Jupiter rules your chart, which gives you that big, generous first impression. The Page of Cups changes the tone without dimming it. Where you'd normally come in laughing, you might come in wide-eyed, curious about people for their own sake. Fire and water are at odds by nature, so the change can surprise you as much as anyone.

People may find you gentler to talk to. You ask about their lives before telling them about yours. You get moved by someone's story in a way that shows. That's still very Sagittarian, because mutable fire loves discovering things, and the Page just points that at people's feelings for a while. You might come across as younger, more innocent, a bit of a student again. Friends may comment on it, and not all of them will know what to make of it. That's worth enjoying.

It helps on trips and in new places, where strangers will tell you their stories. It helps in teaching or study, where you're a better student when you're this open. When you meet someone new, hold back the first opinion that comes to mind and ask a second question.
rising.reversed:
Sagittarius rising with the Page reversed often gets ahead of itself. The bluntness goes out in front and you hurt someone's feelings in the first five minutes, or you come across as naive, over-promising, too eager, telling a new friend they simply have to come travelling with you. Jupiter rules your chart, and in the upside-down version it overdoes the openness without much sense of what the other person wants.

Social events and early dating are where it shows, and work if you're new and trying hard to be liked. Before you make a big friendly gesture to someone you've just met, look at their face and match their pace for a while. You'll still come across as warm, and they'll have room to come towards you.

sun.upright:
Capricorn Suns often grew up early. You're cardinal earth, ruled by Saturn, and you tend to take yourself and your responsibilities seriously from a young age, and to measure yourself by what you've built. The Page is about as young as the deck gets, a court card that hasn't learnt to be serious yet. That sounds like a clash, yet water and earth are actually friendly elements. Water softens earth and earth gives water a shape, and something planted in this pairing tends to take hold.

So the card gives you permission to want something soft. A creative project with no obvious return. A relationship where you're not the responsible one. Some play. Capricorns are famous for getting younger as they get older, and this can be one of the stages of that. The Devil is Capricorn's card among the Majors, a card about what keeps us stuck, and for a Capricorn Sun that's quite often the need to look competent at all times. You might notice how much of your week goes on that.

At work it could be an idea you've dismissed as unprofessional that's actually good. With family it could be a new ease with a parent or a child. Give an hour a week to something you're a total beginner at, and put it in the diary like a meeting so it happens.
sun.reversed:
The soft side has been put away for so long you've forgotten it's there. That's the usual story with a Capricorn Sun and this Page reversed. You're working, coping, being reliable, and a small creative wish or a tender feeling keeps getting pushed to next year. Saturn rules Capricorn, and with the card upside down its discipline can turn into a kind of dryness where nothing's fun because everything's a task.

It can also make you awkward with feelings, other people's especially. A friend cries and you offer a plan. Work is too busy to enjoy, and at home someone wants you to play and you can't find the switch. Say yes to one silly thing, a game with a child, a pottery class, a day with no list. Capricorn gets good at play very quickly once it lets itself.

moon.upright:
A Capricorn Moon keeps its feelings under management. You're not cold. You learnt early that it was safer to cope, and you feel secure when you're competent and things are in hand. Saturn rules your Moon's sign, cardinal earth, and it gives your feelings a sturdy container. The Page of Cups pours something young into it. Earth and water get on, so this is a gentle draw, and the container holds.

What comes up might be from childhood. An old feeling about being looked after, or not being looked after. A memory of a time you were allowed to be silly. You might find yourself unexpectedly soft with a child, or a pet, or an ageing parent, and not quite know why. Capricorn Moons often carried more than their share when they were young, and a card like this can let some of that younger feeling out, very quietly, in a way you can manage. It tends to come out a little at a time, which suits you.

It'll probably show in your body, as tiredness finally catching up with you, or shoulders that want to drop. It'll show at home, too, in wanting comfort you'd normally think you hadn't earned. Let someone make you a cup of tea and bring it to you, and don't get up to help.
moon.reversed:
With a Capricorn Moon, a reversed Page usually means a feeling that's been filed under later and left there. You're fine. You're busy. You've got it handled. Meanwhile a small sadness or longing is making you short-tempered, or making you work harder than you need to. Saturn rules your Moon's sign and it's very good at postponing, and this card upside down suggests the postponing has gone on long enough.

Sleep often shows it, waking early and starting on the day's problems in your head. Family shows it too, where you take charge of everything and then feel nobody looks after you. Tell one person, plainly, that you're tired and could use some help, and let them do it their way.

rising.upright:
Most people meet Capricorn rising and assume you're in charge. Saturn rules your chart, and your usual first impression is composed and capable, a bit reserved, someone who has things in hand and won't waste anyone's time. The Page of Cups softens that. Water and earth are friendly elements, so there's no clash, and people see a warmer, slightly younger version of you, someone who looks curious and maybe a little shy.

You might notice you're less formal with strangers. You laugh at yourself in a meeting. You show enthusiasm for an idea before you've checked it's a good one. Cardinal earth likes to start things with a plan, and the card brings in a different way of starting, following interest and seeing where it goes. That can feel unprofessional to you. From the outside it reads as approachable, and people who'd usually be a bit wary of you might start coming over.

At work that helps with younger colleagues or clients who need to feel you're on their side. In dating, where your reserve can put people off early, it helps even more. The next time you're excited about something, let it show on your face and in your voice, and leave off the sensible caveat.
rising.reversed:
Stiffness is the usual giveaway when Capricorn rising gets this card reversed. You're shy or unsure, so you fall back on the professional manner, the good posture, the short answers, and people read it as coldness or judgement. Saturn rules your chart, and in this upside-down version it armours a feeling you'd be better off letting show.

First meetings bring it out, and social things where you don't know anyone, and new relationships where you're slow to warm up and the other person takes it personally. Sometimes it's the reverse, a sudden awkward attempt at being casual. Say one unguarded thing early on, that you're nervous, or that you love the place, and let people respond to the person under the posture.

sun.upright:
Aquarius Suns usually like a bit of distance. You're fixed air, ruled by Saturn and in the modern view by Uranus, and you're at your best thinking about ideas, groups, the way things could be. Close personal feelings you'd rather look at from a slight angle. This card doesn't have any angle. It's completely taken up with one small surprising thing. Air and water don't clash, though they also don't mix without help, so the card asks you to do the introducing yourself.

What might be going on is a sentimental streak you don't often show. You care about someone more than you've let on. You've got a creative idea that's personal and a bit soppy, which isn't your usual style. The Star is Aquarius's Major, a woman pouring water out under the night sky, and it's the most hopeful card in the deck. There's some of that hope here, only at a smaller scale, for yourself and the people closest to you. Fixed air can be stubborn about staying cool, and this is a good time to let that go a little.

In friendship, it might mean getting properly close to one person. In your work, it could be a project that means something to you personally. Tell someone you've missed them, if you have, and leave it at that without explaining why.
sun.reversed:
An Aquarius Sun with the Page reversed tends to push the detachment too far. Someone offers you a tender moment and you make an observation about it. You feel something and immediately start theorising about why people feel things. Fixed air can hold a position for a long time, and here the position is being slightly above your own feelings, which can go on for months if nobody calls it.

The flip side is a sudden, private sensitivity you don't know how to handle, feeling hurt by a friend's offhand comment and saying nothing. Both turn up in friendships and in whatever groups you belong to. Next time something lands, say that it hurt a bit, out loud. Aquarius Suns are usually surprised by how well people take it.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon handles feelings best from a little distance. You need space, you need to feel free inside your relationships, and you tend to work out what you feel by thinking about it, often in the abstract. That's fixed air, ruled by Saturn with Uranus as the modern ruler. This card brings a feeling right up close. There's no distance in it at all. Water and air don't fight, and they have no natural rapport either, so your Moon has to find its own way to let this one in.

It might be a soft spot for someone that's making you feel exposed. It might be a wave of fondness for your oldest friends. It might be something from childhood coming back, a sensitivity you thought you'd grown out of. Fixed air can resist a feeling for a long time out of sheer principle. What tends to help an Aquarius Moon is treating the feeling as interesting, which it is, and letting curiosity do the work that closeness usually would.

With friends, it could be a late-night conversation where you say more than you planned. In your body, it could be a need for more sleep, or restless nerves. When a feeling surprises you, get curious about it the way you would about someone else's, and ask it a couple of questions.
moon.reversed:
When this card is reversed on an Aquarius Moon, the feeling gets frozen out. You go cool and a bit distant, explain your mood in terms of something sensible, and keep your friends at arm's length without quite meaning to. Fixed air holds its ground, and the reversed Page is a young feeling that's been told to wait. Sometimes the opposite happens and you swing into an oddly intense attachment you can't reason your way out of.

Friendships feel it first, as you pull away without saying why, and so does sleep, which goes light and broken. Pick one friend and tell them honestly how you've been. An Aquarius Moon usually finds it easier once it's been said to someone who won't make a fuss.

rising.upright:
Strangers often find Aquarius rising friendly but hard to place. You're open, a bit unusual, interested in ideas, and there's a slight coolness, as if you're watching the room from a step back. Saturn rules your chart, with Uranus as the modern co-ruler, and fixed air gives you a steady, independent way of meeting people. The Page of Cups warms that up. Water and air need an introduction, and this card makes one, bringing some tenderness into how you come across.

You may seem more earnest. Your oddness, and Aquarius rising usually has some, turns endearing and a bit dreamy. People may tell you things because you seem so interested. You might dress or behave in a way that's sweet and a little eccentric, which suits you. There's a pull between the part of you that wants to stay detached and the part that's genuinely moved by the people in front of you, and that pull is quite visible to others.

In groups, you might be the one new people drift towards. A casual acquaintance could turn into a real friend. At work, your ideas may land better because people can hear that you care. Let one conversation go somewhere personal. Ask what someone loves, and listen to the answer all the way through.
rising.reversed:
Aquarius rising with the Page reversed tends to look aloof, even when you're feeling fragile underneath. You go quiet and watchful at parties, crack a dry joke when someone's being sincere, and people decide you're not interested. Saturn rules your chart, and in this reversal it builds a bit of a wall. A lot of Aquarius rising people are shyer than they look, and the card upside down makes the shyness read as distance. Or you overshoot and come across as oddly intense with a new person, too much too soon.

It shows in groups, in meetings, and in early dating, anywhere first impressions count. When someone opens up to you, skip the clever response. Say something simple and warm, like 'that sounds hard' or 'I'm glad you told me', and let the silence afterwards be fine.

sun.upright:
There's a fish in the Page's cup, poking its head out to look at the young person holding it, and Pisces is the sign of the fishes. You could hardly ask for a closer match. Pisces is mutable water, ruled by Jupiter and in the modern view by Neptune, and it's one of the three signs this court card is made from. With a Pisces Sun, the Page is your own element at its most wide-eyed. It speaks your language, and it turns everything up.

What you're building in yourself is an imagination with somewhere to go. Pisces Suns are often creative, compassionate, porous to other people's feelings, and a bit vague about where they end and someone else begins. The Page adds a fresh spark, a new idea, a new sensitivity, maybe a new artistic or spiritual interest, and it all feels very alive. The risk is the doubling. Mutable water spreads, and with this card on top you can end up with ten beautiful beginnings and no middles. The Moon is Pisces's own Major, a card of dreams and half-light, so you know this territory, and you know how easy it is to wander off into it.

In creative work the ideas may come thick and fast. With someone you care for, your sympathy will flow freely, and it's worth checking it's going somewhere good. Choose one of the new ideas and give it a small, boring structure, a set time twice a week, so it has a chance to grow.
sun.reversed:
A Pisces Sun with this Page reversed can drift. You've got plenty of feeling and plenty of imagination and not much sense of what to do with either, so you daydream, scroll, start things and lose interest. Mutable water spreads when nothing holds it, and the doubled element can leave you unsure who you are for a while. Sometimes it's oversensitivity instead, soaking up everyone's mood and going under.

You'll find it in creative work that stays in your head and in relationships where you've taken on someone else's problems. Pick one small practical thing each day, a walk, a meal cooked properly, one finished page, and do it before anything else. Pisces is steadier than it looks once it has a bit of routine.

moon.upright:
Pisces Moons pick up everything. You feel the mood of a room before you've taken your coat off, you cry at other people's weddings, and you need a lot of quiet time to let it all drain away. Your Moon is in mutable water, ruled by Jupiter and Neptune, and this card is water too, from inside its own home ground. So nothing foreign is arriving. It's more of what's already there.

That can be lovely. Your intuition might be sharp, your dreams vivid, your read on other people very accurate. Creative ideas may turn up in the shower or when you're half asleep. But mutable water with its own element doubled can lose track of whose feelings are whose. You might come away sad from a friend's phone call and not realise the sadness was theirs. That's the too-much side of the pairing, and it's common with Pisces Moons, so don't read anything worrying into it.

In your body it tends to show in sleep, which you need plenty of, and in needing time alone after company. With friends and family, you may be the one everyone brings their troubles to. Before you pick up the next heavy conversation, ask yourself if you've got room for it, and if you haven't, say so.
moon.reversed:
The Page reversed on a Pisces Moon usually means too much feeling and nowhere solid to put it. You might be absorbing other people's moods without noticing, then feeling low and not knowing why. Or you're escaping, sleeping too much, living in a daydream, avoiding a conversation by drifting away from it. Mutable water doesn't like hard edges, and this reversal is what happens when there aren't any.

It shows at home, in your sleep, and in any relationship where you do most of the emotional carrying. Get your hands into something physical, a garden, bread dough, a swim, anything with a clear beginning and end. Then make a short list of whose feelings you've been holding lately, and hand a few of them back.

rising.upright:
People find you easy to talk to and hard to pin down, which is Pisces rising all over. You have a way of reflecting back whatever they bring, and that's why so many of them feel you understand them. Most people remember your eyes, or your voice, more than anything you said. Jupiter rules your chart, with Neptune as the modern ruler, and your rising sign sits inside this card's own zone. So the Page of Cups doesn't change your mask much. It makes it more so.

You look open, young, gentle and very approachable. Strangers may confide in you on the bus. Creative people may want to work with you. Someone might fall for a version of you that's mostly their own idea, which happens a lot with Pisces rising and happens even more with this card. It can be flattering and tiring at once. Mutable water adapts to whatever it meets, and with the element doubled you might find you're adapting before you've noticed you've done it.

It's a lovely card for creative work and for any job where people need to feel safe with you, teaching, nursing, the front desk. In a new friendship, give people one clear fact about yourself early on, a firm opinion or a thing you won't do, so they have something real to hold on to.
rising.reversed:
Blurry edges are the trouble for Pisces rising with this card reversed. You're so busy picking up what everyone else wants that you disappear a bit, and people come away with a nice feeling and no real idea who you are. Or the softness tips into looking lost, vague about plans, late, easily hurt by a brusque stranger. Jupiter and Neptune rule your chart, and neither is much help with limits.

New jobs can bring it out, where people underestimate you, and so can dating, where you might go along with things you don't want. Walk into the next new situation with one clear intention, even a tiny one, like 'I'll ask about the pay' or 'I'll leave by nine', and stick to it.

1.upright:
Your body and your bearing belong to the first house, how you come through a door, how you start things, what people see before you speak. It's an angular house, one of the four corners of the chart, so whatever lands here tends to be visible. Aries is its natural sign and Mars its natural ruler, which makes it fire territory, and the Page of Cups is water. The two elements are opposed, so a card of shy, open feeling has turned up in the part of the chart that's usually about pushing forward.

Mostly that looks like a softer way of starting things. You're less guarded in how you present yourself, a bit younger in manner, readier to be surprised. People can tell what you're feeling from your face. Mercury has its joy in this house, the planet of messages, and the Page has always been a messenger, so there's often a piece of news or a first conversation that sets something going. The friction is that the Mars part of you wants to be brave and decisive about it, and may feel a bit embarrassed by all the sweetness.

In your body, it can mean a need to rest and soften, gentler exercise, a new look that feels more like you. In new situations, it can mean being openly curious in a way people warm to. Try a small change to how you present yourself, a colour or a style you've been drawn to, and see how it feels to walk around in it.
1.reversed:
In the first house the reversed Page tends to show as touchiness right on the surface. Every look feels like a comment, every comment feels personal. This is Mars's house by nature, and with a water card upside down in fire territory you get a lot of steam, moods that flare and then sulk, a face that gives everything away when you'd prefer it didn't.

A fresh start can stall here too, a new you that stays an idea. Your energy may be low or restless, and people react to how you walk into a room. Take care of the basics, sleep, food, fresh air, before you judge how you look or how you're coming across. Most of the touchiness eases once you're rested.

2.upright:
Money you can actually count, and the worth you feel you have, both live in the second house. What you earn, what you own, what you think you deserve. It's succedent, a house about building up and holding on, with Taurus as its natural sign and Venus as its natural ruler. Water and earth get on well, so this Page is a friendly visitor. Something soft and new comes into the money picture, and it has a decent chance of growing.

Often it's a hunch about value. A creative skill someone would pay for. An idea for a small side income that starts as a hobby. It can also be about spending, a pull toward beautiful or sentimental things, which Venus in its own house will always encourage. The tension is between feeling and sense. The Page follows its nose, and the second house wants to know how it adds up, and both have a point. Then there's self-worth, and there's often a tender shift in how you value yourself, a sense that what you make or who you are is worth more than you'd assumed.

With your finances, it suits starting something small and seeing if it grows, and it doesn't suit big emotional purchases. With your sense of yourself, it's worth noticing who makes you feel valued and who doesn't. Put a price on one thing you do for free, even if you never charge it, and see how that number feels.
2.reversed:
Upside down in the second house, the Page tends to blur money with mood. You spend when you're sad, or you avoid looking at your bank balance because it feels like a judgement on you. Venus is the natural ruler here and likes comfort, and a reversed card of young feeling can mean comfort bought on credit. Another version is a creative idea for earning that never gets costed out, so it stays a nice thought.

It shows in your accounts, obviously, and in your sense of what you're worth, which can dip for no clear reason. Sit down with the numbers once, calmly, with a cup of something, and write down what's actually there. Then decide one thing to change and leave the rest for another day.

3.upright:
Messages are this card's oldest meaning, and the third house is where messages live. Texts, emails, conversations with siblings and neighbours, short trips, anything you're learning. It's a cadent house, where things get processed and adjusted, and its natural sign is Gemini, ruled by Mercury. The Moon has its joy here, and the Moon rules Cancer, one of the water signs this card belongs to, so the Page is more welcome in the third than you'd guess. Water and air still need introducing, though.

In this house the Page's message is often literal. A tender note. A text from a brother or sister you haven't heard from in a while. A chat with a neighbour that goes somewhere unexpectedly personal. It can also be a class or a book that moves you. The tension is that Mercury's house wants to explain things and the Page wants to feel them first, so you might find yourself lost for words at moments you'd usually be quick.

With siblings there may be a softening, an old joke that turns into a real apology. With learning, it favours something creative, writing, drawing, music. Send the message you've half-written in your head, even if it comes out a bit clumsy.
3.reversed:
When the Page lands reversed in the third house, words get stuck. You write the message and delete it. You say the wrong thing to a sibling and then sulk about it. Or you read a whole story into a short reply, which is easy to do when a feeling card turns up upside down in a house ruled by Mercury. It tends to be minor, and it tends to feel much bigger than it is.

Texts and emails are the obvious places, and family group chats, and conversations with neighbours or colleagues that feel slightly off. A creative writing idea might stay unstarted because you're worried it'll sound silly. Say the thing out loud to yourself first, and then write it the way you'd say it. Short and a bit awkward is fine.

4.upright:
The fourth house is home in every sense, the actual house or flat, the family you grew up in, whoever shares the house with you, the private ground you go back to at the end of the day. It's angular, a corner of the chart, and its natural sign is Cancer, with the Moon as natural ruler, so this is water territory. The Page is water too, and Cancer belongs to the card's own family of signs. Nothing pushes back, which means it amplifies, the good and the too-much.

The good is tenderness. You might want to make your home softer, warmer, more your own. You might feel closer to a parent, or understand something about your childhood that's been sitting there unexamined. There can be a new arrival of some kind, a baby, a pet, a housemate, someone young who brings a lighter feeling into the place. The too-much is nostalgia and moodiness, old family feelings stirred up and not always easy to settle once they're moving. Angular houses make things visible, so what's going on at home may be obvious to everyone.

With family, it favours small gestures, a phone call, cooking the dish your grandmother made. At home, it favours something you make or choose yourself, a picture on the wall, a plant. Do one thing that makes your home feel more like the place you'd want to come back to.
4.reversed:
In the fourth house a reversed Page tends to mean family moods. Someone at home is sulking, or you are, and nobody's quite saying what it's about. Old feelings from childhood can come up sideways, as a flash of hurt at a parent's offhand comment, or a sadness that arrives when you visit the house you grew up in. The Moon rules this house naturally, and with water doubled and turned over, the feeling floods in private.

You'll feel it in how you are with the people you live with, and in family calls that leave you flat. Sometimes it's simply not wanting to be at home much at all. Pick one person in the family and have a short, honest, kind conversation about something small. It often clears more than you'd expect.

5.upright:
Play is the whole point of the fifth house. Romance, flirting, creativity, hobbies, children, anything you do just because it's fun. Leo is the sign that naturally goes with it and the Sun is its ruler, and Venus rejoices here, so it's a warm, pleasure-loving house. The Page of Cups fits it in spirit and clashes with it in element. The card is water and the house is fire, and those two are opposed, so the delight here comes with a streak of shyness.

Think of the first flutter of a crush, where you're thrilled and also want the floor to swallow you. Or a creative thing you've started, painting, music, a bit of writing, that you love and can't quite bring yourself to show anyone. Fire wants to perform and the Page wants to stay quietly absorbed, and you may swing between the two.
